patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Jira and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Jira and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Jira only if your buying job matches “Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.15/user/mo ” rather than Notion's shape. Choose Notion only if your buying job matches “Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo ann” rather than Jira's shape. Workflow advantage: Jira leans project-tracking; Notion leans team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Jira and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Jira is Atlassian Agile issue tracker for software teams — Free ≤10; Standard from ~$8.15/user/mo annual.; Notion is Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo annual; AI on Business..
- Company-size focus: Jira (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Notion (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Jira-leaning project-tracking vs Notion-leaning team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Jira — Steep learning curve outside engineering; Notion — Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management.

Limitations — Jira: Steep learning curve outside engineering; Confluence often required for wiki/docs depth; Notion: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management; Reporting/dashboards thinner than dedicated PM tools.

Poor-fit cases: Jira is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Steep learning curve outside engineering · Notion is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management · Avoid Jira if you actually need Notion's motion (Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/u)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
